concepts.name: Histological Subtype (Squamous)
concepts.rationale: Squamous cell histology is a known prognostic factor in NSCLC.

concepts.name: Performance Status
concepts.rationale: ECOG/Performance status is a primary driver of treatment response and survival.

concepts.name: Neurological/Brain Involvement
concepts.rationale: Clusters suggest imaging features of intracranial lesions/edema.

concepts.name: Pain Management (Opioids)
concepts.rationale: Requirement for morphine indicates higher symptom burden/disease progression.

concepts.name: Gastrointestinal Symptom Profile
concepts.rationale: Absence of nausea may correlate with better baseline tolerance or lower disease burden.

concepts.name: Dosage/Medication Fragments
concepts.rationale: N-grams represent fragmented medication dosing instructions rather than clinical states.

concepts.name: Social/Caregiver Context
concepts.rationale: Template artifacts related to social history or caregiver presence.

concepts.name: Clinical Documentation Artifacts
concepts.rationale: Phrases are common linguistic fillers or structural elements of clinical notes.

assessment: The most credible effect modifiers are Histological Subtype, Performance Status, and Neurological/Brain Involvement, as they represent established clinical determinants of NSCLC outcomes. The 'Pain Management' cluster is a plausible proxy for disease severity. The majority of other high-ranking n-grams (dosage fragments, social history, and linguistic fillers like 'is dominated by') are high-likelihood artifacts of clinical note-taking and template structure.
